structured_output.hypothesis: In North Sea plaice, Fulton's condition factor K = 100*W/L^3 computed from individual fish rises with length class to a single maximum near 30 cm (the size at onset of maturity) and then declines at larger sizes.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using individual-fish length (cm) and weight (g) from DATRAS plaice (Pleuronectes platessa) records, mean K per 2-cm length class (classes with n>=30) shows: (a) a single peak class within 25-35 cm; (b) mean K at the peak exceeds mean K in the 10-15 cm classes by at least 5%; and (c) mean K in the 45-55 cm classes is lower than the peak by at least 3%, with Spearman rho < -0.5 between class-mean K and length across classes above the peak.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if the peak K class lies outside 25-35 cm, or if K is flat (peak differs by <3% from both the 10-15 cm and the 45-55 cm classes), or if K rises monotonically (Spearman rho > 0 above 35 cm) or falls monotonically across the whole size range.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's k = W/L^3 is Fulton's condition factor (scaled by 100 with W in g, L in cm). 'Steadily increases to a maximum, then slowly declines' is operationalised as a unimodal curve of class-mean K against length. Sexes and seasons are pooled as in Thompson's data, with a sensitivity check by quarter. 'About 30 cm, the size at which maturity begins' is operationalised as a peak within 25-35 cm; modern North Sea plaice L50 varies by sex and era, so the maturity link is tested only through the peak location window (optionally cross-checked with the Maturity field). Caveat: the DATRAS individual-weight field may be sparsely populated for plaice in some surveys; if fewer than 5000 fish with weight are available, the test is inconclusive.

dataset.publisher: International Council for the Exploration of the Sea (ICES)
dataset.why_it_fits: DATRAS provides North Sea survey (NS-IBTS, Beam Trawl Survey) biological sampling records (CA exchange format) for plaice (Pleuronectes platessa), including individual length class, individual weight, sex, maturity and quarter. Fields used: LngtClass, IndWgt, Sex, Maturity, Quarter, Year; K = 100*IndWgt/(length in cm)^3 per fish.
